text:
sara.dev: FYI customer (AcmePayments) is seeing intermittent 502s on hosted API during long-lived streaming calls after ~25-35s of idle. They can repro locally with curl. Ticket #INC-3891 attached.

mike.sre: Can you paste the minimal repro curl and any request IDs or edge logs? Is this only streaming or normal requests too?

sara.dev: Only observed on server-sent streaming / chunked responses so far. Customer gave this curl loop: 

```bash
# open a stream, wait, then re-request over same connection
for i in 1 2 3; do \\
  curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -N 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream' || true; \\
  sleep 30
done
```

They see first request succeed, then the 2nd request returns 502 with: 

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
server: envoy
date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:02:10 GMT
content-length: 0
x-request-id: rwd-req-12345
```

leo.backend: Do we have the edge traces for x-request-id rwd-req-12345? Also which upstream returned the 502 (auth/billing/model-router)?

sara.dev: Attached edge logs snippet from the customer time window: 

```
[edge] 2025-05-14T15:02:09Z conn=10.4.2.3:62134 upstream=10.10.12.8:443 state=reset reason=idle-timeout
[edge] 2025-05-14T15:02:10Z request=rwd-req-12345 status=502 upstream_status=-
```

anya.product: Interesting that the conn reset shows idle-timeout on upstream IP. Could be upstream (model router) closing keepalive too aggressively, then envoy treats it as 502 when client reuses the connection.

mike.sre: Agreed. Two quick asks: (1) can infra produce tcpdump on the edge-to-upstream path to confirm RST/FIN at 30s, (2) what's our current envoy upstream_idle_timeout and nginx keepalive settings in hosted?

infra-bot: Metrics: https://console.redwood.ai/apps/edge/requests?query=502&from=2025-05-14T15:00Z to=2025-05-14T15:10Z — spike aligned with customer's repro. Current envoy upstream_idle_timeout = 15s for that host pool, nginx keepalive_timeout = 20s.

leo.backend: Looks like our upstream_idle_timeout < customer idle (30s). That will cause envoy to close connection and subsequent pooled reuse will hit 502. We should bump idle timeout on the pool and/or detect broken pools and refresh.

mike.sre: Quick mitigation: add a canary config to increase upstream_idle_timeout to 60s for the affected pool, and enable envoy's connection_reuse_strategy to avoid reusing closed connections (force TCP health-check or drain). Also add a retry for idempotent streaming handshake?

sara.dev: Will propose that to infra and ask Acme to test again tomorrow. Any repro tips I can send them?

mike.sre: Send the curl loop but reduce sleep to 20s and after each failed request capture tcpdump: 

```bash
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w dump.pcap host 10.10.12.8 and port 443 &
# run curl repro
kill %1
```

Look for `RST` flags from upstream. If RST at ~15-20s then upstream closed early. If FIN then graceful close.

leo.backend: Also check the model-router and auth service logs for connection limits and keepalive settings. There was a recent JVM change that reduced netty idle timeout in the auth service.

anya.product: For the customer update: explain we found mismatched keepalive/idle timeouts between edge and upstream causing connection resets on reuse, and we're testing a config canary to extend idle timeouts and make reuse safer. Offer a temporary client-side workaround: close connection after stream rather than reuse (curl `--no-keepalive`).

sara.dev: Customer confirmed they can repro with my modified curl (added `--no-keepalive`) and the errors stop. I'll schedule canary tonight.

mike.sre: Nice. After canary, we'll monitor 502 rate and also add an automated test hitting long-lived streams with simulated idle.

leo.backend: Postmortem actions: 1) align default upstream_idle_timeout with typical streaming idle (60s), 2) add health check to invalidate connection pool on upstream close, 3) update docs for recommended keepalive settings for on-prem upstreams.

sara.dev: Filing follow-up ticket ENG-7842 for config canary + tests. Will update here when canary is live. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #INC-3891 updated: status -> investigating.

mike.sre: Thanks team — keep me looped if logs show different error (504 vs 502).

sara.dev: Can confirm canary deployed at 2025-05-14T23:10Z, initial metrics look good (502 spike subsided). Closing the loop with Acme now.

anya.product: Great work, please include the short customer-facing blurb and the ENG-7842 plan in the follow-up so we can reuse in runbooks.
